question: What is the freezing point of water on the Celsius scale?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0ºC**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The freezing point of water on the Celsius scale is **0ºC**.
 
• The Celsius scale, also known as the centigrade scale, is a temperature scale used by the International System of Units (SI).
 
• On this scale, the freezing point of water is 0 degrees Celsius, and the boiling point is 100 degrees Celsius, under standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• The Celsius scale is widely used around the world for most temperature measuring purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Celsius scale was named after the Swedish astronomer **Anders Celsius**, who developed a similar temperature scale.
 
• Before being widely adopted, various temperature scales like Fahrenheit and Kelvin were also used for different purposes.
 
• The Celsius scale is particularly convenient for scientific calculations and everyday temperature measurements.
 
• In the Fahrenheit scale, the freezing point of water is 32ºF, and the boiling point is 212ºF.
